title: Record a deed or search land records
question: I need to record a deed, deed of trust or other land document in Staunton. What is required?
office: Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office (Clerk of the Circuit Court, an elected constitutional officer); the City Assessor updates the land book after recording
summary: Deeds, deeds of trust and other land documents for property in the City of Staunton are recorded by the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office, 3rd floor, 113 E. Beverley Street, not by the Augusta County court. Staunton requires a Virginia Land Record Cover Sheet, made with the state's online generator. Present the signed, notarized original before 4:30 p.m. with fees and taxes paid, or e-record through Simplifile or CSC iRecord. Expect recording fees of $18 to $52 by page count, an $8 technology fee, a $20 processing fee when recordation tax is due, $5 more for a paper filing, the state recordation tax plus Staunton's one-third city tax, and a grantor tax on sales. Land records back to 1802 can be viewed at the office (most visitors must leave phones and laptops in free storage at the entrance), or online for $420 a year.

steps.step: Make sure the land is in the City of Staunton, so the document goes to the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk
steps.who: Whoever presents the document (settlement agent, attorney, lender or owner)
steps.how: A deed, deed of trust or other land document is recorded in the clerk's office of the city or county where the land lies. Land in the City of Staunton is recorded with the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office. Staunton is an independent city surrounded by Augusta County, which has its own circuit court clerk, so a Staunton mailing address does not prove the land is in the city: check the parcel in the city's GIS maps or on the tax bill. Recording matters: an unrecorded deed or deed of trust does not protect against later buyers for value without notice or against lien creditors, and protection runs only from the time of recording.
steps.deadline: No fixed deadline to record, but protection against later buyers and lien creditors starts only when the document is recorded
steps.quote: shall be void as to all purchasers for valuable consideration without notice not parties thereto and lien creditors, until and except from the time it is recorded in the county or city in which the property subject to such contract, deed, or bill of sale is located.

steps.step: Prepare the deed or deed of trust to Virginia's recording standards
steps.who: The attorney or party who prepares the document (an owner may prepare their own deed)
steps.how: Under Va. Code § 17.1-227, deeds and deeds of trust must be prepared according to the requirements of §§ 55.1-300 and 55.1-316, whose model forms (which may be followed 'or to the same effect') name the parties, state the consideration, describe the property and, for a deed, name the city or county where it lies. Do not refer to the specific portion of a recorded restrictive covenant that restricts ownership or use in a way § 36-96.6(A) of the Virginia Fair Housing Law prohibits; the clerk may refuse such a deed (§ 55.1-300). On a sale, state the consideration (price) on the first page; no deed subject to the grantor tax is recorded without it. Give the parcel (tax map) number on the first page or in the cover sheet, and name the law for any tax exemption claimed. Remove any Social Security number, and make sure each name to be indexed is legible. Where no cover sheet is used, the clerk may reject a writing unless surnames are underscored or in capitals and each grantor and grantee is named in the first clause, every page is numbered, and the consideration, value and exemption law appear on its face. Staunton requires a cover sheet, so that rejection power does not apply there, but meeting those points is still good practice. For a deed conveying a home with up to four units, the first page must also name the title insurance underwriter (or say the preparer does not know of title insurance) and say that the owner, or a Virginia attorney named with a State Bar number, prepared it; the preparer statement does not apply to deeds of trust. To claim the exemption from recordation tax, a deed of gift, a quitclaim deed without consideration or a deed to correct a fraudulently recorded deed must say so in the deed, and a deed of distribution must say so on its front page; a transfer on death deed without consideration is exempt as well. A subdivision plat cannot be recorded until the city's subdivision agent has approved it.
steps.quote: shall be prepared according to the requirements for deeds and deeds of trust as set forth in §§ 55.1-300 and 55.1-316 , as applicable.

steps.step: Sign the document and have each signature acknowledged before a notary
steps.who: Each grantor (seller or borrower) who signs; a notary public
steps.how: The clerk records a writing for each person who signed it with an original signature, once that person has acknowledged it or two witnesses have proved it. A document that appears on its face to have been properly notarized under the Virginia Notary Act is presumed properly notarized and must be recorded if it otherwise meets the requirements.
steps.quote: shall record any such writing as to any person whose name is signed thereto with an original signature, when it shall have been acknowledged by him, or proved by two witnesses as to him in such court, or before such clerk

steps.step: Make the Virginia Land Record Cover Sheet, which Staunton requires
steps.who: The attorney, settlement agent or party presenting the document
steps.how: Staunton's Clerk requires a cover sheet with every land record. The Clerk's page links the Supreme Court of Virginia's Virginia Land Record Cover Sheet (VLRCS) Generator, set to Staunton; its page says the Staunton court requires a cover sheet for any deed or other instrument about an interest in real property. In the generator you fill in tabs for the content, grantors, grantees and parcels, accept its Terms and Conditions of Use, and print the cover sheet as a PDF (you can also save and reload an XML file). The blank Form CC-1570 is the same cover sheet on paper; the Clerk's page points only to the online generator, and whether the Clerk accepts a hand-completed CC-1570 was not confirmed. It lists the grantors and grantees, consideration, actual value, any tax exemption and the law for it, the parcel number, and the name and address to return the recorded document to. Whoever prepares it is responsible for its accuracy, and the clerk may rely on it. Read the Clerk's own 'requirements for cover sheets' document as well (form f3; its contents are not described here). A required cover sheet is not counted as a page for the recording fee.
steps.fee: None for the cover sheet; it is not counted as a page for the recording fee when the clerk requires it
steps.quote: To file a land record, you must produce a cover sheet with your document.

steps.step: Work out the fees and taxes with the state Deed Calculation tool
steps.how: The Circuit Court Deed Calculation tool from the Office of the Executive Secretary of the Supreme Court of Virginia estimates recording fees and taxes. Choose STAUNTON CIRCUIT COURT, the instrument type (for example DBS, deed of bargain and sale, or DOT, deed of trust), the consideration and value, and the page count, and say whether it is a paper submission. For Staunton the tool says the court requires a cover sheet and adds $5 for each land record filed on paper. Staunton's Clerk page also points to Va. Code §§ 58.1-801 and 58.1-802 for the value rules on a deed of bargain and sale. For help, the tool says to call the circuit court and ask for the record room or deed section (Staunton Clerk's Office: 540.332.3874).
steps.fee: See Fees: recording $18 to $52 by page count, $8 Technology Trust Fund fee, $20 deed processing fee when recordation tax is due, $5 paper-filing fee, state and city recordation taxes, grantor tax on sales and the $1 transfer fee
steps.quote: STAUNTON CIRCUIT COURT adds a fee of $5.00 per instrument for every land record filed by paper pursuant to Va. Code §17.1-258.3:1

steps.step: Choose to record on paper at the Clerk's Office or electronically through Simplifile or CSC iRecord
steps.who: Settlement agent, attorney, lender or owner
steps.how: The Clerk's page says land records are also accepted electronically through two third-party e-recording services, Simplifile and CSC iRecord, and links their websites; to start, contact the service (the Clerk's page gives their phone numbers). A clerk with an e-recording system follows the Uniform Real Property Electronic Recording Act. Paper filing stays allowed under state law, but Staunton adds $5 for each land record filed on paper. The e-recording services' own fees were not found.
steps.fee: $5 per land record filed on paper (none stated for e-recording, apart from the services' own charges, which were not found)
steps.quote: Land records are also accepted electronically through Simplifile and CSC iRecord.

steps.step: Present the original with the cover sheet at the Clerk's Office and pay the fees and taxes before 4:30 p.m.
steps.who: Settlement agent, attorney, lender or owner; Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office
steps.how: Bring the signed original and its cover sheet to the Clerk's Office on the 3rd floor of the George M. Cochran Judicial Center, 113 E. Beverley Street (open 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday). Transactions that need payment must be done before 4:30 p.m. No deed, deed of trust or other instrument is recorded until its taxes and fees are paid. The grantor tax is the seller's unless the parties agree otherwise, and the clerk certifies on the deed that it was paid. The clerk may ask for an affidavit or other evidence of the price, the value or a claimed exemption, and knowingly misstating the price is a Class 1 misdemeanor. If you pay by credit or debit card, the clerk must add a convenience fee of no more than 4 percent of the payment or a flat $2 per transaction; Staunton's amount was not found. Portable electronic devices (phones, computers, smart watches) are not allowed in the courthouse except for listed groups such as attorneys, and other visitors only when the Sheriff decides they pose no security risk and need the device for their work at the courthouse or their case; free storage is provided at the security entrance, at the owner's risk. Whether the office accepts recordings by mail, and which payment methods it takes, were not found; call 540.332.3874.
steps.deadline: Before 4:30 p.m. on a weekday for any transaction that requires payment
steps.fee: Recording $18 (10 or fewer pages), $32 (11 to 30) or $52 (31 or more), plus the taxes and fees listed under Fees
steps.quote: All transactions requiring payment must be done before 4:30 p.m.

steps.step: The Clerk records the document and indexes it under each grantor and grantee
steps.how: The clerk endorses the day and time of recording on the document, records it in the deed book, and indexes it under the names of the grantors and grantees (and may also index it by parcel number). Indexing in the daily index or the general index happens immediately upon recording, and entries in the daily index must be moved to the general index within 90 days. If a document is not recorded on the day it is delivered, the delivery is time-stamped, and for priority against later buyers and lien creditors that stamp is presumed to be the recording time, unless the clerk decides the requirements for recording were not met.
steps.deadline: Indexed immediately upon recording (daily or general index); moved to the general index within 90 days after recording
steps.quote: Upon admitting any such writing or other paper to record, the clerk shall endorse thereon the day and time of day of such recordation.

steps.who: Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office; the grantee or the person named on the cover sheet for return
steps.how: Once recorded, the original may be returned to the grantee, unless the document or the cover sheet clearly names someone else with a current address. The cover sheet (Form CC-1570) has a 'Recording Returned To' section for this. The state fee schedule notes that some clerks' offices ask for a copy of the document, or charge 50 cents a page, when the recorded original is wanted back immediately. How and when Staunton returns originals was not found; ask the Clerk's Office.
steps.quote: Some clerk's offices require the recording agent to provide a copy of the document being recorded, or to pay an additional $0.50 per page for copying the document if immediate return of the recorded document is requested.

steps.step: The Clerk reports the sale, and the City Assessor updates the owner on the land book
steps.who: Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office; City Assessor; City Treasurer
steps.how: Each month the clerk sends copies of the recordation receipts for the previous month's deeds of conveyance (not deeds of trust), with the grantee's address, to the commissioner of revenue (the statute's term) and the Virginia Department of Taxation. The land book must then show the new owner and the property address, or another address the new owner gives in writing for future tax bills. In Staunton the City Assessor posts the land book and gives the Treasurer the list of parcels and the taxes they owe; which office takes a written billing-address request was not found, so ask the City Assessor or the Treasurer. The state's cover sheet guide (Form CC-1570 instructions) says the grantee address entered on the cover sheet is the address the tax bill will be sent to. The clerk collects the $1 land book transfer fee from the new owner at recording.
steps.deadline: The clerk forwards receipts before the 15th of each month for deeds recorded in the previous month
steps.fee: $1 transfer fee, paid by the new owner and collected by the clerk at recording
steps.quote: the commissioner shall ensure that the land book is updated to reflect the grantee and property address or any such other address as may be specified in writing by the grantee for the delivery of future tax bills.

steps.step: Settle this year's real estate tax at closing; bills follow the January 1 assessment
steps.how: Staunton bills real estate tax on the assessment as of January 1. Bills usually go out in early May, with 75 percent due June 20 and the rest December 5; bills paid from a mortgage escrow are due in full June 20. The city pages read do not say how the tax for the year of sale is split between buyer and seller, or how a parcel sold during the year is re-billed; settle the split at closing and ask the City Treasurer about the bill.
steps.deadline: Real estate tax due June 20 (75 percent) and December 5 (25 percent)
steps.quote: Tax bills based on the current calendar year assessment (January 1) are usually sent in early May.

steps.step: Search land records in person at the Clerk's Office
steps.who: Anyone; Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office
steps.how: Records kept by the circuit court clerk, including the deed books and their indexes, are open to inspection by any person in the clerk's office, and the daily index is kept there for public examination. Staunton's land records go back to 1802. The Clerk's Office is on the 3rd floor of the Cochran Judicial Center, 113 E. Beverley Street, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays. The Clerk's Visitor Information page says phones, tablets, computers and other electronic devices are not permitted in the building, and the court's device policy lets in only listed groups, such as attorneys, and others the Sheriff approves because they need the device for their work at the courthouse; free storage is provided at the security entrance. Even a permitted device may not be used to take photographs without a judge's prior written authorization, so plan to take notes on paper or order copies. Parking is in the New Street and Johnson Street garages, at the Augusta Street and Hardy metered lots, or along Beverley Street; the accessible entrance is at the rear, with parking on New Street.
steps.fee: Free to inspect; copies $0.50 a page, certificate and seal $2
steps.quote: You may visit the Clerk's office to view land records dating back to 1802.

steps.step: Ask the Clerk for copies or certified copies of land records
steps.who: Anyone; Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office
steps.how: Ask the Clerk's Office in person, by phone (540.332.3874) or by email to the office mailbox. Copies are 50 cents a page (or per image), and the clerk's certificate with the court seal is $2 more. The clerk may require the request in writing with your name and legal address, and may ask for a deposit. The records must be provided within a reasonable time, and no later than 30 days after a complete request. Records kept by the clerk as custodian are outside the Virginia Freedom of Information Act and are requested under Va. Code § 17.1-208; the Clerk's own FOIA policy page also says FOIA does not apply to records the clerk keeps as custodian and that public records kept by the clerk may be requested from the clerk of court.
steps.deadline: Within a reasonable time, and no later than 30 days after a complete request (Va. Code § 17.1-208(F))
steps.fee: Copies $0.50 per page or image; certificate and seal $2
steps.quote: Public records maintained by a clerk of a circuit court, including nonconfidential court records maintained in individual case files, may be requested from the clerk of court.

steps.step: Search online through Secure Remote Access by yearly subscription from the Clerk
steps.who: Subscriber; Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office; Office of the Executive Secretary (runs SRA)
steps.how: Staunton's land records can be searched online through the state's Secure Remote Access (SRA) system. Each user must fill in the Clerk's application and sign a user agreement, then mail them to the Circuit Court Clerk with payment. The cost is $420 per year per user, paid in advance. Statewide, viewing images is limited to subscribers a local clerk has authorized; clerks who turn on free index-only access show as 'Available' on SRA's Available Courts tab, and whether Staunton has done so was not checked. SRA data may not be resold or reposted, and in-person access stays available.
steps.fee: $420 per year per user, payable in advance
steps.quote: Each user must submit an application and sign a user agreement.

steps.step: Look up ownership, parcel numbers and land books from the City Assessor
steps.how: The City Assessor's page links the city's real estate database and GIS maps for individual parcels, and posts unofficial PDF land books (2023, 2025 and 2026). The land book is made each year and lists each owner's name, the legal description, the parcel number, the assessed value and the tax levied. These assessment records help find the parcel number for the cover sheet and point to the recorded deed, but they are not the deed itself. The Assessor's Office is on the first floor of City Hall, phone 540.332.3827.
steps.quote: The land book, which is created yearly, contains property record information, including the property owner's name, legal description, parcel number, assessed value and levied tax amount.

steps.step: Optionally, sign up for VADeed Alert to be told when a document in your name or parcel number is recorded
steps.who: Property owner; Office of the Executive Secretary (runs VADeed Alert)
steps.how: The Clerk's Office encourages owners to sign up for VADeed Alert, a free, voluntary state service. It sends an email when a document matching your name or Parcel ID number is recorded, which can give early warning of deed fraud or unauthorized filings. The page links the sign-up on the state's VADeed Alert site (risweb.vacourts.gov).
steps.quote: VADeed Alert sends email notifications when certain documents are recorded in the land records that match your name or Parcel ID number (PID).

fees.item: Recording and indexing a deed, deed of trust or other land document (plats no larger than 8.5 x 14 inches count as pages; a cover sheet Staunton requires does not)
fees.amount: $18 for 10 or fewer pages; $32 for 11 to 30 pages; $52 for 31 or more pages. $3.50 of each fee is designated for preserving the circuit courts' permanent records, administered by The Library of Virginia; the state fee schedule shows the fee as $14.50, $28.50 or $48.50 plus that $3.50.
fees.quote: $18 for an instrument or document consisting of 10 or fewer pages or sheets; $32 for an instrument or document consisting of 11 to 30 pages or sheets; and $52 for an instrument or document consisting of 31 or more pages or sheets.

fees.amount: Not counted as a page for the recording fee, because the Staunton clerk requires it
fees.quote: The cover sheet may be recorded with the deed or other instrument with which it is submitted, but it shall not be included as a page for determining the amount of any applicable filing fees pursuant to subdivision A 2 of § 17.1-275 except in the case of a cover sheet submitted pursuant to subsection B.

fees.item: Oversize plat or map sheets (larger than 8.5 x 14 inches)
fees.quote: A fee of $17 per page or sheet shall be charged with respect to plat or map sheets larger than eight and one-half inches by 14 inches.

fees.amount: $8 per instrument recorded in the deed books (raised from $5 on July 1, 2026). Not charged on documents tendered by a federal, state or local government.
fees.quote: the clerk of each circuit court shall assess a fee of $8, known as the "Technology Trust Fund Fee," in each civil action, upon each instrument to be recorded in the deed books

fees.item: Deed processing fee (Appropriation Act § 3-6.01, as listed in the state fee schedule)
fees.amount: $20 on a deed or deed of trust when state recordation tax is assessed (the state fee schedule says not to charge it on documents tendered by an agency of the Commonwealth)
fees.quote: Deed Processing Fee (Charged on Deeds and DOTs when tax under §§ 58.1-801 or 58.1-803 is assessed).

fees.amount: $5 per land record filed on paper. The state Deed Calculation tool lists this fee for the Staunton Circuit Court.
fees.quote: Any clerk of a circuit court with an electronic filing system established in accordance with this section may charge a fee not to exceed $5 per instrument for every land record filed by paper.

fees.item: State recordation tax on a deed (often called the grantee tax)
fees.amount: 25 cents per $100 (or part of $100) of the price or the property's value, whichever is greater. Value means the most recent tax assessment.
fees.quote: The rate of the tax shall be 25 cents on every $100 or fraction thereof of (i) the consideration of the deed or (ii) the actual value of the property conveyed, whichever is greater.

fees.item: State recordation tax on a deed of trust or mortgage
fees.amount: 25 cents per $100 (or part of $100) of the debt secured (for a credit line, the maximum that may be outstanding). A refinance of a debt secured by a deed of trust on which the tax was already paid is taxed at 18 cents per $100 on the first $10 million (Va. Code § 58.1-803(E)); the refinancing deed of trust must certify the deed book and page or instrument number of the instrument on which the tax was paid. Rates step down above $10 million.
fees.quote: a recordation tax on deeds of trust or mortgages is hereby imposed at a rate of 25 cents on every $100 or portion thereof of the amount of bonds or other obligations secured thereby.

fees.amount: One-third of the state recordation tax, on the first recordation of each taxable instrument in the city (Staunton City Code § 3.25.010), collected by the Clerk and paid into the city treasury (§ 3.25.020). For land partly outside the city, the city tax is figured only on the part in the city (also Va. Code § 58.1-3801). The one-third is figured on the state grantee tax, not on the grantor tax: § 58.1-802 says it authorizes no increase in the local recordation tax, and the state fee schedule computes the local grantee tax as one-third of the state amount.
fees.quote: the council of any city and the governing body of any county may, pursuant to Chapter 38 (§ 58.1-3800 et seq.) of this title, impose a city or county recordation tax in an amount equal to one-third of the amount of state recordation tax.

fees.amount: 50 cents per $500 (or part of $500) of the price or value, whichever is greater, not counting liens that stay on the property, when that amount is over $100. Paid by the seller unless the parties agree otherwise. Half goes to the state and half to the city. Not charged on a deed of trust or other instrument securing a debt (Va. Code § 58.1-811(C)(2)).
fees.quote: shall be 50 cents for each $500 or fraction thereof, exclusive of the value of any lien or encumbrance remaining thereon at the time of the sale

fees.amount: $1, paid by the new owner and collected by the clerk at recording
fees.quote: For making an entry transferring to one person lands before charged to another, one dollar, which shall be paid by the person to whom the transfer is made

fees.amount: $3 per deed or deed of trust, only where the Virginia Outdoors Foundation holds open-space easements. Whether it applies in Staunton was not confirmed; the Deed Calculation tool applies it per court.
fees.quote: there is hereby imposed a $3 fee on every deed, deed of trust, contract, or other instrument admitted to record in those jurisdictions in which open-space easements are held by the Virginia Outdoors Foundation.

fees.item: Credit or debit card convenience fee
fees.amount: A convenience fee the clerk must collect on card payments, no more than 4 percent of the payment or a flat $2 per transaction (the state fee schedule also allows the greater of $2 or a percentage up to 4 percent). The Staunton Clerk's fee for recordings was not found.
fees.quote: Such convenience fee shall not exceed four percent of the amount paid for the transaction or a flat fee of $2 per transaction.

fees.amount: $0.50 per page (or per image for an electronic record)
fees.quote: a fee of $0.50 for each page or, if an electronic record, each image.

fees.item: Clerk's certificate and court seal on a copy (certified copy)
fees.quote: For annexing the seal of the court to any paper, writing the certificate of the clerk accompanying it, the clerk shall charge $2

fees.item: Secure Remote Access (online land records) subscription
fees.amount: $420 per year per user, payable in advance (state cap: $50 a month per subscriber plus a per-image fee no higher than the $0.50 copy fee; a clerk may instead run a program of up to $2 per transaction plus a per-image fee, Va. Code § 17.1-276(C); any Staunton per-image fee was not found)
fees.quote: The cost is $420 per year per user, payable in advance.

fees.item: Deed of gift, quitclaim without consideration, or deed correcting a fraudulently recorded deed
fees.amount: No recordation tax when no consideration passed (the deed must say so). Recording fees still apply. Transfer on death deeds without consideration are also exempt (Va. Code § 58.1-811(J)), and so are deeds of distribution without consideration, which must say so on the front page (§ 58.1-811(K)).
fees.quote: No recordation tax shall be required for the recordation of any deed of gift, quitclaim deed, or deed to correct a fraudulently recorded deed, including a deed of trust, between a grantor or grantors and a grantee or grantees when no consideration has passed between the parties.

escalation.trigger: The Clerk turns the document away for a missing or incomplete cover sheet, or for missing names, page numbers, consideration or exemption
escalation.next: Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office: correct the document or the cover sheet (the VLRCS Generator can reload a saved file) and present it again
escalation.quote: Circuit court clerks may require that any deed or other instrument conveying or relating to an interest in real property be submitted for recordation with a cover sheet detailing the information contained in the deed or other instrument necessary for the clerk to properly index such instrument.

escalation.trigger: The Clerk refuses to record a document that meets the legal requirements (for example, one that appears properly notarized, has its cover sheet, and has its taxes and fees paid)
escalation.next: Staunton Circuit Court: petition for a writ of mandamus against the clerk (venue is the city where the record or proceeding is, Va. Code § 8.01-261(5); a petition verified by oath, served on the clerk a reasonable time before the application, Va. Code § 8.01-644)
escalation.quote: in other cases in which it may be necessary to prevent the failure of justice and in which mandamus may issue according to the principles of common law

escalation.trigger: A request for land records or copies gets no answer within 30 days of a complete request
escalation.next: A written follow-up to the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office; if the records are still withheld, a mandamus petition in the Staunton Circuit Court (Va. Code § 17.1-513). These clerk's records are outside the Virginia FOIA, so the FOIA Council and the FOIA petition do not apply (Va. Code § 2.2-3703(A)(6)).
escalation.deadline: The clerk has no more than 30 days from a complete request
escalation.quote: but in no event longer than 30 days from the date of a complete request made by a requester that is fully compliant with the requirements of this section and other applicable law.

escalation.trigger: The Clerk says the old record has been transferred to The Library of Virginia for permanent archiving
escalation.next: The Library of Virginia, which is then the custodian and answers requests for those records
escalation.quote: the Library of Virginia shall be the custodian of such permanently archived records and shall be responsible for responding to requests for such records.

escalation.trigger: The Clerk denies or ends a Secure Remote Access subscription
escalation.next: Inspect the records in person at the Clerk's Office, which stays open to the public whatever happens to online access
escalation.quote: Nothing herein shall be construed to require the use by the general public of the secure remote access to land records made available by the clerk, and such records may continue to be accessed in person in the clerk's office.

escalation.trigger: You believe the state recordation or grantor tax collected at recording was wrong (for example, an exemption was refused or the wrong value was used)
escalation.next: Tax Commissioner, Virginia Department of Taxation: application for correction (whether this covers recordation taxes collected by a clerk was not confirmed; see caveats)
escalation.deadline: Within 90 days from the date of the assessment (Va. Code § 58.1-1821). The sections read do not say when a recordation tax collected by the clerk counts as assessed; § 58.1-1812(A) says only that a recordation tax return is considered filed on the date of recordation.
escalation.quote: Any person assessed with any tax administered by the Department of Taxation may, within ninety days from the date of such assessment, apply for relief to the Tax Commissioner.

escalation.trigger: The Tax Commissioner denies relief, or you go straight to court over the state tax
escalation.next: Circuit court application to correct an erroneous state tax assessment
escalation.deadline: Within three years from the assessment, or one year from the Tax Commissioner's determination, whichever is later
escalation.quote: within (i) three years from the date such assessment is made or (ii) one year from the date of the Tax Commissioner's determination under § 58.1-1822 , whichever is later, apply to a circuit court for relief.

escalation.trigger: You believe the City of Staunton recordation tax (the one-third local share) was wrongly charged
escalation.next: Staunton Circuit Court: application to correct an erroneous local tax assessment, with the City of Staunton as a party (applicability to a recordation tax collected by the clerk not confirmed; see caveats)
escalation.deadline: The later of three years from the last day of the tax year, or one year from the date of the assessment (Va. Code § 58.1-3984(A))
escalation.quote: apply for relief to the circuit court of the county or city wherein such assessment was made.

escalation.trigger: You disagree with the city's assessed value (it sets future real estate taxes and is the value used for recordation tax)
escalation.next: City Assessor's Office (informal review), then the Board of Equalization, then the Staunton Circuit Court. See the separate real estate assessment appeal process.
escalation.deadline: Informal appeals for 30 calendar days from the mailing of the notice of assessment, then a further 30 days for formal written appeals to the Board of Equalization
escalation.quote: The Assessor's Office accepts informal appeals for 30 calendar days from the date of the mailing.

escalation.trigger: After recording, the land book or tax mailing address still shows the old owner or the wrong address
escalation.next: City Assessor's Office (keeps the land book, which must be updated from the clerk's monthly recordation receipts); give any different billing address in writing
escalation.quote: the commissioner shall ensure that the land book is updated to reflect the grantee and property address or any such other address as may be specified in writing by the grantee for the delivery of future tax bills.

escalation.trigger: A recorded deed or deed of trust has an obvious error in the property description (for example a wrong lot number or plat reference)
escalation.next: A Virginia attorney may record a corrective affidavit with the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk, after giving the parties notice and 30 days to object (Va. Code § 55.1-609(C), (D)); otherwise a corrected deed
escalation.deadline: The affidavit may be recorded if no written objection arrives within 30 days after notice is delivered
escalation.quote: Obvious description errors in a recorded deed, deed of trust, or mortgage purporting to convey or transfer an interest in real property may be corrected by recording an affidavit in the land records of the circuit court for the jurisdiction where the property is located or where the deed, deed of trust, or mortgage needing correction was recorded.

escalation.trigger: A deed was recorded fraudulently against your property
escalation.next: Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office: record a deed to correct the fraudulently recorded deed (no recordation tax when no consideration passes); get legal advice on further court action, and use VADeed Alert to watch for new filings
escalation.quote: No recordation tax shall be required for the recordation of any deed of gift, quitclaim deed, or deed to correct a fraudulently recorded deed, including a deed of trust, between a grantor or grantors and a grantee or grantees when no consideration has passed between the parties.

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) refuses automated readers, so the city pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The Deeds & Land Recordings page's newest copy is of 2026-05-11; its text matches the copies of 2025-11-15 and 2021-11-12 except for an added CSC iRecord phone line in 2025. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them or by phone before you act.

Not confirmed: the Clerk's 'requirements for cover sheets' PDF (form f3) and the Secure Remote Access application and user agreement (form f4). Neither has an Internet Archive copy, and the city site refuses automated readers. Their titles and URLs come from the Deeds & Land Recordings page; any Staunton-specific cover sheet rules, SRA terms, payment methods or mailing instructions in them are not reflected here.

Local practice not found: whether the Clerk's Office records documents sent by mail, which payment methods it accepts and its card convenience fee for recordings, its daily recording cut-off beyond the 4:30 p.m. payment rule, whether documents are recorded the same day, how and when originals are returned, and what Simplifile and CSC iRecord charge. Ask the Clerk's Office (540.332.3874). The Clerk of Circuit Court page also notes a convenience fee for online payments of court fines and costs; that note is not about recordings.

Cover sheet effect. Under Va. Code § 17.1-223(A) the clerk's authority to reject a writing for the listed format points (names in the first clause, page numbers, consideration and value, exemption) applies 'unless a cover sheet is submitted'. Because Staunton requires a cover sheet, those points may not be grounds for rejection there, but other rules still apply on their own: the consideration on the first page for a deed subject to the grantor tax (§ 58.1-802(A)), the title insurance and preparer statements for homes of up to four units (§ 17.1-223(B)), the parcel number (§ 17.1-252), no Social Security numbers (§ 17.1-227) and a legible indexing name (§ 55.1-604). The steps recommend meeting all of them. How the Staunton Clerk applies this was not confirmed.

The Clerk's page says to 'Log in' to the Supreme Court of Virginia's portal to create a cover sheet. The generator's landing page, read on 2026-10-11, asked for no login; it says the user must accept its Terms and Conditions of Use before the cover sheet can be submitted. Only the landing page was read; no cover sheet was made.

The Deed Calculation tool's data for Staunton ('Court requires a cover sheet.' and the $5 paper-filing fee) sits in the court list's option data on the page, not in visible body text. No calculation was run. Augusta County Circuit Court is listed separately there: it does not require a cover sheet and also charges the $5 paper-filing fee.

Local ordinance: Staunton's City Code is published on General Code's eCode360, whose Terms and Conditions of Use limit its content to personal use and forbid reproducing it for public purposes, so no City Code text is quoted here. In lexflow's paraphrase, § 3.25.010 imposes a city recordation tax of one-third of the state recordation tax collectible under Va. Code §§ 58.1-800 through 58.1-813 on the first recordation of each taxable instrument in the city, figured only on the city part of land that lies in more than one locality, and § 3.25.020 has the Clerk collect it and pay it into the city treasury. eCode360 warns its copy may not reflect the latest legislation; confirm with the Clerk of Council or the Clerk's Office.

Fee figures differ between Office of the Executive Secretary (OES) sources. The Deed Calculation help text gives $14.50, $28.50 and $48.50 by page count and $20 per oversize plat. Va. Code § 17.1-275(A)(2) gives $18, $32 and $52 and $17 per oversize sheet. The fee schedule (Appendix C, rev. 07/26) reconciles the page fees as $14.50, $28.50 or $48.50 plus the $3.50 Library of Virginia share, and oversize plats as $13.50 plus $3.50 ($17), so the help text's $20 plat figure looks out of date.

The Technology Trust Fund fee is $8 in the index text of Va. Code § 17.1-279 (2026, c. 966), and Appendix C says it rose from $5 on July 1, 2026. The $20 deed processing fee comes from the Appropriation Act (§ 3-6.01) as listed in Appendix C; the Act itself was not read.

Va. Code § 17.1-258.3:1 (the $5 paper-filing fee and the right to file on paper) is marked 'Effective until July 1, 2027' in Open US Law's copy of the Code of Virginia, which holds no successor text. Re-check it on or after July 1, 2027. The Deed Calculation help text describes the fee as a charge on documents 'recorded electronically', which does not match the statute as read (a fee on paper filings where the clerk has e-filing).

Large transfers: Appendix C shows a state recordation tax scale that steps down above $10 million (25, 22, 19, 16 and 13 cents per $100) for deeds as well as deeds of trust. In the index text, § 58.1-803(F) sets that scale for deeds of trust and § 58.1-801(A) gives a flat 25 cents for deeds. This matters only for very large transfers; ask the Clerk. The regional transportation fees in Appendix C (Northern Virginia, Hampton Roads, WMATA) apply only in those regions, not in Staunton.

Whether the $3 open-space preservation fee (§ 58.1-817) applies in Staunton, which depends on whether the Virginia Outdoors Foundation holds open-space easements in the city, was not confirmed. The Deed Calculation tool decides this for each court.

Secure Remote Access: $420 a year is $35 a month, within the state cap of $50 a month per subscriber. Whether Staunton charges a per-image fee, and whether it has enabled free index-only searching on SRA, were not checked (SRA's Available Courts list sits inside a web application that was not used). The Clerk's page has given the same $420 figure since at least November 2021.

FOIA: land records held by the circuit court clerk are outside the Virginia FOIA (Va. Code § 2.2-3703(A)(6)), and the Clerk's own FOIA policy page says FOIA does not apply to records the clerk keeps as custodian. Requests go under Va. Code § 17.1-208, so the Virginia public-records ladder (FOIA Council opinion, FOIA mandamus heard within 7 days) does not apply. The Clerk's FOIA page lists charges for FOIA requests ($0.50 per page, $5 for a CD or flash drive and $17.50 an hour for staff time); whether the Clerk applies the hourly rate to land record requests was not found, and the statutory copy fee is $0.50 a page. No statute giving a specific appeal from a clerk's refusal to record was found; the mandamus route under § 17.1-513 is the general common-law remedy, and whether it fits a given refusal is a legal question.

Recordation tax disputes: whether the Tax Commissioner route (§ 58.1-1821) and the circuit court route (§ 58.1-1825) cover recordation taxes collected by a clerk was not confirmed in the sections read; § 58.1-1812(A) treats a recordation tax return as filed on the date of recordation, which suggests the Department of Taxation administers the state tax. Whether § 58.1-3984 reaches the city's share collected by the Clerk, and whether Staunton City Code ch. 3.55 (Refunds of Taxes, not read) applies, were not confirmed either.

Land book hand-off: Va. Code § 58.1-3303 says the clerk sends recordation receipts to the commissioner of the revenue. In Staunton the City Assessor keeps the land book (City Assessor page) and gives the Treasurer the parcel and tax list (Real Estate Tax FAQs). The exact hand-off, how long the update takes, and how a mid-year sale is re-billed were not found.

Venue: Staunton is an independent city surrounded by Augusta County, which has its own circuit court and clerk. Some properties with a Staunton mailing address lie in Augusta County. Check the parcel's jurisdiction before recording. For land in both, the state taxes are paid where the instrument is first recorded, and the second office collects only its local recordation tax (Va. Code § 58.1-812(A)); each locality's tax covers only its part of the property (§ 58.1-3801). The Deed Calculation tool lists Augusta County as not requiring a cover sheet.

Building rules: the Visitor Information page says electronic devices such as phones, tablets and computers are not permitted in the building. The Staunton Circuit Court's Policy Regarding Portable Electronic Devices (court order adopted 6/10/2026, posted on vacourts.gov) revokes earlier court device policies. It bars portable electronic devices from the courthouse except for attorneys; law enforcement, probation officers and magistrates on duty; judges; City and State employees with credentials who work there or are on official business; court reporters; Department of Forensic Science employees attending as witnesses; interpreters; and other visitors the Sheriff decides pose no security risk and need the device for their work at the courthouse or their case. Permitted devices must be silent, and photographs or recordings need a judge's prior written authorization. Free storage is provided at the security entrance, and the Sheriff is not liable for loss or damage. The policy is a scan with no text layer, so it was read as an image and is paraphrased. The City's own linked device policy document (not archived) was not read.

Privacy: the city pages and the vacourts.gov court page name the elected Clerk and other staff, and the Clerk's FOIA page and the Assessor's page give named staff and personal mailboxes. The court's device policy is signed by a judge. None of these names is recorded. The only email given is the role mailbox circuitcourtclerk@ci.staunton.va.us, published on the City's Public Records Request page for land recordings and deeds. The phone numbers and mailbox the Clerk's page gives for Simplifile and CSC iRecord belong to private companies and are not recorded as contacts. The Clerk's fax line (540.332.3970) is published but left out, as in the other Staunton files.

Not covered: releases of deeds of trust (certificates of satisfaction, forms CC-1501 and CC-1505), mechanic's liens, subdivision plat approval (an unapproved subdivision plat cannot be recorded, Va. Code § 15.2-2254(5)), the details of transfer on death deeds, and the title examination itself. Whether a non-attorney may lawfully prepare a deed for someone else is a question of unauthorized practice of law and is not covered here. This is legal information, not legal advice.

Cover sheet guide: the OES Virginia Land Records Cover Sheet Guide (Rev. 9/25) was read for this check. Its page headers carry the words 'CONFIDENTIAL - CLERK'S OFFICE USE ONLY' although it is published as the CC-1570 instructions on vacourts.gov, so it is paraphrased here, not quoted. It says that when a court does not require a cover sheet its pages are added to the page count, which does not apply in Staunton.

corrections: Quotes: all 118 original quote instances are verbatim. The 101 state-law quotes are substrings of I.text_of for the cited section with whitespace normalised only, and their subsection labels match the index text; lexflow's matcher (places.check_quotes) reports 101 of 101 before this check and 112 of 112 after it. The 17 local and procedure quotes were matched word for word against Internet Archive captures fetched read-only with the research User-Agent (Deeds & Land Recordings 2026-05-11 and 2025-11-15, Clerk of Circuit Court 2026-05-07 and 2026-07-21, FOIA policy 2025-11-14, VADeed Alert 2026-05-13, City Assessor 2026-09-16, Real Estate Tax FAQs 2026-06-15) and against live reads of the Deed Calculation page (the STAUNTON CIRCUIT COURT option data) and the OES fee schedule, Appendix C rev. 07/26. www.ci.staunton.va.us still answers 403, robots.txt included, and was not fetched further. Eleven state-law quotes were added (§§ 55.1-300, 55.1-407(A)(2) and (A)(3)(c), 17.1-223(B), 58.1-812(A), 58.1-803(E)(2), 58.1-811(K), 58.1-3801, 17.1-275(A)(27), 17.1-276(C), 8.01-261(5)), each confirmed the same way. Phrases quoted inside step text and caveats ('Log in', 'requirements for cover sheets', 'or to the same effect', 'Recording Returned To', 'Court requires a cover sheet.', 'recorded electronically', 'Available') were also found in their sources.

Archive copies: caveat 2 called the 2025-11-15 Deeds & Land Recordings capture the newest; a 2026-05-11 capture exists, with the same body text. Steps s4, s6, s12 and s14 now cite it. The 2026-05-11 timestamps cited for the FOIA policy and Visitor Information replay the 2025-11-14 and 2025-11-15 captures; s13 now cites the capture actually served, and s7 cites the 2026-07-21 Clerk capture, which still carries the 4:30 p.m. rule.

Step s2: 'must follow the state's forms' overstated § 17.1-227, which requires preparation according to the requirements of §§ 55.1-300 and 55.1-316, whose forms may be followed 'or to the same effect'; reworded. Added the § 55.1-300 rule that the clerk may refuse a deed referring to the specific portion of a prohibited restrictive covenant (new legal_basis). The step said a transfer on death deed 'must say so' to be exempt; § 58.1-811(J) has no such requirement. A deed of distribution must say so on its front page (§ 58.1-811(K), new legal_basis), and a deed to correct a fraudulently recorded deed joins the § 58.1-811(D) list. The § 17.1-223(A) format points (names in the first clause, page numbers) are now stated as rejection grounds only where no cover sheet is used, and as good practice in Staunton. The preparer statement of § 17.1-223(B)(iii) does not apply to deeds of trust (new legal_basis). The parcel number may go on the first page or in the cover sheet (§ 17.1-252), and a subdivision plat is approved by the city's subdivision agent (§ 15.2-2254(2)).

Step s4: 'The blank Form CC-1570 is the same cover sheet on paper' read as an accepted alternative; the Clerk's page points only to the online generator, so the step now says acceptance of a hand-completed CC-1570 was not confirmed.

Step s7 and the card fee row: 'may carry a convenience fee' understated § 17.1-275(A)(27), under which the clerk 'shall collect' one on card payments (new legal_basis). The device rule was refined from the Staunton Circuit Court's Portable Electronic Devices Policy (court order adopted 6/10/2026, vacourts.gov; a scan read as an image and paraphrased): attorneys and other listed groups may bring devices, the Sheriff may allow others who need one, and free storage is provided at the security entrance. Step s12, the summary and the building-rules caveat were updated to match; s12 adds that photographs need a judge's prior written authorization.

Step s8: the time-stamp presumption left out the § 55.1-407(A)(3)(c) exception ('unless the clerk determines that the applicable requirements for recordation of the instrument have not been satisfied') and its limit to priority under subdivision 1; both added, with § 55.1-407(A)(2) for indexing immediately upon recording (new legal_basis entries). Deadline text adjusted.

Step s10: 'the local assessing official' is now the statute's 'commissioner of revenue'. 'Write to the City Assessor if tax bills should go to a different address' was on no page read (§ 58.1-3303(B) says only 'specified in writing'), so it now says to ask the Assessor or the Treasurer. Added that the OES cover sheet guide uses the grantee address on the cover sheet for the tax bill.

Step s13: 'the Clerk's own FOIA policy page says the same' overstated the page, which does not cite § 17.1-208; it now says what the page says. Step s16: 'creating an account' is not on the page; reworded to the page's sign-up link.

Fees: the $3.50 share is now worded as § 17.1-275(A)(2) puts it (designated for preserving the circuit courts' permanent records, administered by The Library of Virginia). Deed processing fee: not charged on documents tendered by an agency of the Commonwealth (Appendix C). Deed of trust: a refinancing deed of trust must certify the book and page or instrument number of the instrument on which tax was paid (§ 58.1-803(E)(2)). City tax: added § 58.1-3801 and that the one-third is figured on the state grantee tax, not the grantor tax (§ 58.1-802(A); Appendix C). SRA: added the § 17.1-276(C) alternative of up to $2 per transaction. Exempt deeds: the deed of distribution front-page statement.

Escalation: the mandamus rung now gives venue, the city where the record or proceeding is (§ 8.01-261(5), new legal_basis). The Tax Commissioner rung's deadline no longer suggests that § 58.1-1812(A) fixes the date of assessment; it says the sections read do not say when a clerk-collected recordation tax counts as assessed.

Caveats, forms and sources: the archive caveat, the building-rules caveat and the venue caveat (state taxes are paid where first recorded and the second office collects only local tax, § 58.1-812(A); each locality taxes only its part, § 58.1-3801) were rewritten; a caveat on the OES cover sheet guide was added; the privacy caveat now notes that the judge who signed the device policy is not named. Form f7 (the CC-1570 guide, Rev. 9/25) was read and retitled. Sources added: the device policy PDF, the CC-1570 guide, and §§ 55.1-300, 8.01-261 and 58.1-3801. The summary now lists the $20 processing fee and device storage.

Confirmed without change: recording in the Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office, the cover sheet requirement and its fee treatment (§ 17.1-227.1(C)), the $5 paper-filing fee in the Deed Calculation data, Simplifile and CSC iRecord, the 4:30 p.m. payment rule and hours, all tax rates, the $1 transfer fee, the 30-day records deadline and the FOIA exclusion, land records from 1802, the $420 SRA fee and its application process, the Assessor's appeal windows, the corrective affidavit route, and the eCode360 paraphrase of City Code §§ 3.25.010 and 3.25.020 (re-read once, not quoted).

Privacy and schema: no staff names, personal mailboxes or direct lines. circuitcourtclerk@ci.staunton.va.us is the office mailbox the City's Public Records Request page gives for land recordings and deeds; 540.332.3874 and 540.332.3827 are the office lines on the Clerk's and Assessor's pages. The JSON is valid, step ids s1 to s16 and form ids f1 to f7 are unique, every referenced form (f1, f2, f4, f5) exists, and the escalation types are in the ladders vocabulary.

Local practice is not published on any page read: recording by mail, payment methods, the card convenience fee actually charged, same-day recording, how originals are returned, and the e-recording vendors' fees.

Whether the Tax Commissioner (§ 58.1-1821) and circuit court (§ 58.1-1825) routes cover state recordation tax collected by a clerk, and whether § 58.1-3984 or City Code ch. 3.55 covers the city share, is unconfirmed; the escalation rungs say so.
Whether the $3 open-space fee (§ 58.1-817) applies in Staunton is unconfirmed; running a calculation would submit the tool's form.
